We are seeking a Marketing Research & Data Analyst with experience in data analysis, AI-driven search analytics, and content strategy to join Flixmedia Ltd as a KTP Associate, based at its London office.

About the role

This is an exciting opportunity to accelerate your career through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP), working at the interface of industry and academia with Flixmedia Ltd and The School of Management at the University of Bath.

As the KTP Associate, you will lead this innovative project to develop an advanced decisioning GEO content optimisation platform that transforms shopper behaviour data into actionable insights. The project will create new data science capabilities that enable global brands and retailers to measure, test and optimise GEO performance and digital content driving improved engagement and conversion outcomes.

You will be embedded within Flixmedia, working closely with company stakeholders while receiving academic support and mentorship from experts at the University of Bath. As project lead, you will take ownership of project delivery, manage key stakeholder relationships and drive the successful implementation of project objectives.

This role offers a unique opportunity to apply cutting-edge research in a commercial setting while gaining valuable experience in leadership, project management and innovation.

About Flixmedia Ltd

Flixmedia Ltd is a leading retail technology company that helps global brands and retailers create, optimise and distribute digital product content that improves online shopper experiences and drives sales. Flixmedia was recently named by the Sunday Times as one of the Best Places to Work, while also being recognised as a UK-certified Great Place to Work.

Benefits of being a KTP Associate:

In addition to the salary, KTP Associates benefit from:

£3,000 dedicated personal development budget
10% of working time allocated to professional development
Two residential training programmes focused on leadership and project management
Mentoring and support from both Flixmedia and the University of Bath
Access to extensive academic and industry resources
Travel and subsistence budget for project-related activities
Mentoring opportunities through Innovate UK Business Connect
Potential opportunity to secure a permanent role following successful project completion
About you

The ideal candidate will have:

A PhD in Marketing with strong quantitative components or a related discipline (including candidates currently in postdoctoral research roles). Alternatively, a relevant Master’s degree combined with three or more years’ experience in quantitative marketing research, analytics or data-driven product innovation 
Experience in data analytics, ideally within marketing, e-commerce or digital content environments, alongside familiarity with cloud platforms, data visualisation, UX principles and digital content management workflows
Strong quantitative research methods skills relevant to marketing, such as experimentation, causal inference, econometrics, and machine learning
Technical skills, including proficiency in R or Python, SQL (preferably BigQuery), and experience with API-enabled digital systems
Ability to translate analytical findings into actionable commercial recommendations
Familiarity with Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) concepts and objectives
Ability to translate business problems into research questions, review and synthesise academic literature, develop rigorous empirical research designs, and interpret findings with appropriate consideration of identification, robustness and limitations
Experience contributing to academic research outputs, such as peer-reviewed publications, working papers or conference presentations.
Strong communication, project management and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work independently, collaborate across academic and commercial teams, and manage complex projects

As a KTP Associate you can enjoy the benefits of being an employee at the University of Bath whilst working full-time at Flixmedia. 

It is essential that you understand how KTP works with business and the University, and the vital role you will play.

Further information

This is a fixed-term role for a period of 18 months.

This is a full-time role, primarily office-based at Flixmedia's London office with the opportunity to work hybrid. Flixmedia offers 24 days of annual leave, plus UK public holidays.

For any questions about this role please email partnerships@bath.ac.uk

postings.title: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researchers - A systematic data assimilation model to predict thermoacoustic instabilities
postings.listing_context: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Early Stage Researchers - A systematic data assimilation model to predict thermoacoustic instabilities Department of Engineering Studentships 9 November 2026 31 December 2026 NM51656
postings.advert_text:
This studentship is one of 15 across Europe in the Marie Curie ITN HyNOISE (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311721)

The overall objective is to optimize the design of hydrogen-fuelled gas turbine injectors, so that combustors are quiet and not susceptible to thermoacoustic instabilities. This requires a quantitatively-accurate model of the thermoacoustic behaviour of the combustor. This model will be obtained by data assimilation from laboratory experiments (NTNU), large eddy simulations (TUB), and industrial experiments (RRD). This data will be assimilated into thermoacoustic models using UCAM's adjoint-accelerated inference and optimization method (AXIOM).

The first intermediate objective is to extend AXIOM to typical hydrogen flame geometries using data from a laboratory scale combustor at NTNU with Bayesian model selection. The second intermediate objective is to extend AXIOM to industrial scale geometries using data from a real gas turbine fuel injector on an industrial test rig at RRD. Bayesian experimental design will be used to identify the experimental configurations that maximize the information that can be learned from a limited number of tests. The third intermediate objective is to develop and test several candidate mean field flame models with TUB and then to assimilate LES data into these models with AXIOM. The result will be a Bayesian framework that transfers data from experiments and numerical simulations into low order models. These models will steadily accumulate data and become more accurate over time. They can therefore be used for optimization and re-optimization, as more data become available in the future.

Research Objectives

-Assimilation of experimental data from a laboratory scale combustor into thermoacoustic models and flame models.

-Assimilation of experimental data from a RRD industrial scale test rig into thermoacoustic models.

-Development and testing of several candidate mean field flame models with TUB.

-Assimilation of LES data into candidate mean field flame models and identification of optimal models.

-Assimilation of experimental data from RRD industrial scale test rig into flame models.

-Optimization of burner design to reduce susceptibility to thermoacoustic instability

Expected Results

-Detailed description of the acoustic field in premixed hydrogen combustion in canonical configurations.

-Creation of a quantitatively accurate thermoacoustic model of the RRD industrial scale test rig containing an industrial burner, able to match experimental results from the RRD rig within quantified uncertainty bounds and able to extrapolate to different configurations within predicted uncertainty bounds.

-Creation of a quantitatively accurate mean field flame model of a turbulent hydrogen flame, able to match the LES results on which it was trained to within quantified uncertainty bounds, and able to extrapolate to unseen LES data.

-Optimal burner design derived from the quantitatively accurate models obtained from outcomes 1 & 2, and a numerical tool for optimizing the design at different conditions and combustor geometries.

Secondments

-Technical University of Berlin (Germany, ca. 2 months): application of developed model to improve mean fields reconstructions of non-measured quantities

-ETH Zurich (Switzerland, ca. 2 months): to check capabilities of LOM to predict indirect noise.

Home, EU, or Overseas

According to the international mobility rules of the MSCA-DN program, the candidates must not have spent more than 12 months in the hosting country (UK), during the 36 months preceding the starting of the PhD.

Applicants must have:

-MSc or equivalent in the field of aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, physics or similar

-Solid knowledge of Fluid Mechanics and Thermodynamics, Computer Science and Informatics (Numerical Analysis; simulation, optimisation and modelling tools; Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD))

-Ability to work efficiently and self-reliantly in a diverse inter-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment

-Ability to work in a team as well as independently

-Ability to solve complex problems with adherence of strict deadlines

-Proactive attitude

-Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal) in English to derive the full benefit from the network training

-As secondments and events are foreseen, applicants must be ready to travel

To apply for this studentship, please send your two page CV and transcripts (if available) to Matthew Juniper (mpj1001@cam.ac.uk) to arrive no later than 31 December 2026.

Please note that any offer of funding will be conditional on securing a place as a PhD student. Candidates will need to apply separately for admission through the University's Graduate Admissions application portal; this can be done before or after applying for this funding opportunity. The applicant portal can be accessed via: www.graduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/egegpdpeg. The final deadline for PhD applications is 13 May 2027, although it is advisable to apply earlier than this.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

 We are looking for a Research Assistant to join the Centre for Finance, Governance and Sustainable Growth within the University of Leicester School of Business, supporting the research project “Artificial Intelligence Adoption, Organisational Transformation, and Labour Market Change” . You will work with the research team to acquire, evaluate and interpret data, undertake high-quality analysis and critical evaluation, and contribute to the development and application of appropriate research methods. You will also support the collection, storage, cleaning and analysis of project data and undertake literature searches to help advance the research. 

 You will contribute to sharing the project’s findings with the research team and to research outputs including co-authored journal articles, technical papers and book chapters. You will have opportunities to participate in workshops and conferences, work with the AICPA & CIMA research team, and collaborate with colleagues nationally and internationally. The Centre for Finance, Governance and Sustainable Growth provides a cross-disciplinary research environment focused on areas including financial markets, fintech innovation and sustainable economic transformation, with partnerships spanning universities, industry, investors, regulators and policymakers.

 You will be at least a second-year PhD student in finance, economics or a related subject and hold a Master's qualification. You will bring relevant research experience, strong econometric skills and practical experience of applying research techniques to produce high-quality outputs to deadline.  You will demonstrate research potential and enthusiasm for the subject area, together with excellent analytical, problem-solving and written and verbal communication skills.  You will join the 2D-MINDs team, led by Dr Soumya Sarkar within the Sustainable Electronic Technologies research group in the School of Electronics and Computer Science (ECS) at the University of Southampton. You will also be part of the interdisciplinary ECS Centre for Neuromorphic Technologies (CeNT).

 The position is funded by the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship “2D semiconductors for intelligent non-volatile memory devices” (2DMINDs) . The post will be full-time for a period until 31/01/2029 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for another 12 months.   You will investigate two-dimensional semiconductors and ferroelectric materials to develop non-volatile memory that co-locates storage and processing for low-power AI hardware. Your research will combine materials characterisation, interface engineering and device fabrication at Southampton Nanofabrication Centre to develop foundry-compatible fabrication protocols alongside specialist electrical and optical characterisation facilities. Training and support will be provided to develop the skills required for your research.

 The role is well suited to candidates who wish to develop their expertise in emerging memory devices and neuromorphic technologies within a supportive, interdisciplinary research environment. We welcome applicants with complementary experimental backgrounds; experience across all the areas listed below is not expected.

 You should be a resourceful and passionate researcher who will plan and conduct experiments, develop measurement techniques and generate high-quality research data. You will contribute to the project’s scientific direction, prepare manuscripts, undertake short research visits to project partners (University of Cambridge, NPL), present findings at international conferences, write project reports and support the supervision of master’s and PhD students.

 The role offers support for conference travel, collaboration, industry engagement and outreach. Extensive leadership training and transferable skills development will support your progression towards research independence and future leadership in ferroelectric neuromorphic devices.

 Essential requirements 

 A PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in materials science, physics, electronic engineering or a related discipline.

 Experience in one or more of the following: fabrication and characterisation of devices based on 2D semiconductors, or ferroelectric materials.

 Strong experimental and analytical skills, with the ability to plan research, interpret results and solve technical problems.

 Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams.

 Desirable experience 

 Ferroelectric transistors, tunnel junctions or diodes, or other non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices.

 E-beam lithography, thin-film deposition or dry-transfer assembly of van der Waals heterostructures.

 Temperature-dependent electrical transport or pulsed electrical measurements.

 Optical spectroscopy, including Raman, photoluminescence or reflectance, or scanning probe microscopy, including AFM, PFM or KPFM.

 Contributing to academic publications, collaborative research or student supervision.

 We warmly welcome applicants from all backgrounds, particularly those underrepresented in the field. ECS holds an Athena SWAN Silver award in recognition of its continued commitment to improving equality for women in science and engineering. We have a range of staff development programmes and a unique mentoring and wellbeing scheme. We recognise that research careers follow different paths and welcome applications from candidates whose PhD completion or career progression has been affected by caring responsibilities, health conditions or other personal circumstances. International applicants are encouraged to apply. Informal enquiries should be directed to Dr Soumya Sarkar ( soumya.sarkar@soton.ac.uk ). 

 Apply by uploading your CV  and a cover letter  detailing how your skills and experience match the requirements of the role.

Job Description - Postdoctoral Research Associate in Environmental Engineering and Microbiology (26001413)
Job Description
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate in Environmental Engineering and Microbiology  (Job Number: 26001413)
Department of Biosciences
Grade 7: - £39,560 to £46,970 per annum
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: 24 Months
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Working Arrangements: 9am and 5pm
Closing Date: 23-Nov-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Not Applicable.
 

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department
Biosciences is one of the very best departments in the UK (2nd Guardian 2027, 4th Complete University Guide 2027) and it has an outstanding reputation for excellence in teaching, research, and the employability of our students. The department provides a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment. 

The Role

Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Environmental Engineering and Microbiology to join CARMA – the Co-selection of Antimicrobial Resistance by Metals Alliance. CARMA is a large, transdisciplinary UKRI-funded research programme investigating how metal pollution in rivers and wastewater co-selects for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and what this means for human health, environmental regulation and intervention. It is a collaboration between colleagues in the UK and India, bringing together Durham University, Imperial College London, the University of Birmingham, the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi and Pondicherry University, with environmental engineers, microbiologists, infection specialists, modellers, economists, genomic experts, patients and practitioners.

This post is based in the Department of Biosciences but has substantial engineering content, focused on water quality, water chemistry and environmental measurement. The post-holder will lead the design and delivery of harmonised environmental sampling at an array of river sites in Northern England, and work with partners in India who are carrying out parallel sampling on the Ganges, Yamuna and near Chennai, so that samples are collected and analysed in the same way at every site.

Working with Professor David Graham and Dr Marcos Quintela-Baluja, the post-holder will develop a structured sampling plan with our Indian partners; oversee sample collection and processing, including culture-based microbiology, metal and water chemistry analyses, DNA extraction and preparation of samples for genomic and metagenomic sequencing; and build a well-organised project archive and database that makes the field data available to all partners. A central part of the role is to act as the interface between field sampling and the project’s bioinformatics, modelling, economics and clinical teams, turning field observations into consistent, well-documented datasets that those colleagues can use. Detailed bioinformatic analysis will be carried out by a second PDRA and by partners elsewhere in the project. Therefore, the role requires working knowledge of metagenomics, bioinformatics, and statistics; modelling and economics can be learned on the job.

The post reports to Professor David Graham and is co-managed by Dr Marcos Quintela-Baluja. Hybrid working is possible. Because the role involves laboratory and field work, the post-holder will normally be expected on site in Durham three to four days a week, although we are happy to discuss flexible arrangements. A full driving licence is required to reach field sites.

Key responsibilities:

To understand and convey material of a specialist or highly technical nature to the team or group of people through presentations and discussions that leads to the presentation of research papers in conferences and publications.
To prepare and deliver presentations on research outputs/activities to audiences which may include research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To publish high-quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify areas for research, develop new research methods and extend the research portfolio.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to form relationships for future research collaboration.
To plan and manage own research activity, research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the planning of research projects.
To deliver training in research techniques/approaches to peers, visitors and students as appropriate.
To interact with and support students involved in project fieldwork and sample processing, including students at partner institutions in India, as appropriate.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.
To engage in continuing professional development by participation in the undergraduate or postgraduate teaching programmes or by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.   
To design, with the Principal Investigator and partners in the UK and India, a structured and harmonised sampling plan for river sediment, water and wastewater samples.
To lead and oversee UK field sampling campaigns across wet and dry seasons, including sample collection, labelling, chain of custody, storage and shipment between sites.
To work with partners in India to ensure that sampling procedures and analytical methods are identical across all sites, including a one-week visit to India early in the post.
To oversee and perform sample processing, including culture-based microbiology (selective plating and multidrug-resistance screening), total and bioavailable metal and water chemistry analyses, DNA extraction, and sample preparation for genomic and metagenomic sequencing.
To jointly supervise, with the Principal Investigator, a research technician, including planning, allocating and checking laboratory and field work.
To create and maintain a structured project archive and database of samples, metadata and results, accessible to partners across the project.
To contextualise field data and organise it into consistent, well-documented formats for colleagues undertaking bioinformatic, modelling, economic, and clinical analyses.
To ensure that field and laboratory work complies with health and safety, risk assessment and research data management requirements.

This post is fixed term for 24 months (anticipated 15 January 2027 to 14 January 2029). The post is funded by a transdisciplinary UKRI research grant (CARMA) and is tied to that time-limited project; funding for the post is available for this fixed period only.

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

Successful applicants will, ideally, be in post by 15th January 2027.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University:

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. 

We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally. There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools. If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Contact Information 

Department contact for academic-related enquiries 

Professor David Graham – david.w.graham@durham.ac.uk

Dr Marcos Quintela-Baluja – marcos.quintela-baluja@durham.ac.uk

Contact information for technical difficulties when submitting your application 

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to fos.recruitment@durham.ac.uk   

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).  

How to Apply  

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. It will be at the discretion of the recruiting panel as to whether they will also consider any desirable criteria, but we would urge candidates to provide evidence for all criteria.  

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.  

Submitting your application 

We prefer to receive applications online. We will update you about your application at various points throughout the selection process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to make sure you have not missed any of our updates.

What to Submit 

All applicants are asked to submit: 

Your CV 
A cover letter which details your experience, skills, and achievements in meeting (or the potential to meet) the essential criteria set out in the person specification of the job description.
A supporting statement (no more than two pages) explaining how your experience meets the essential criteria, with particular emphasis on hands-on field sampling, culture-based microbiology and metal/water chemistry analysis, and giving examples that show your ability to organise and manage complex work (e.g. sampling campaigns, sample archives or datasets).

Next Steps 

Short-listed candidates will be invited to the University, either virtually or in-person, and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the project team. The assessment will last approximately 45 minutes: a 10-minute presentation, followed by questions on the presentation and an interview. In the presentation, candidates should briefly introduce themselves and their experience, then outline how they would design a harmonised sampling plan across the UK and Indian sites and organise the resulting field data so that it can be used by bioinformatics, modelling, economic and clinical colleagues. We anticipate that interviews will take place in December 2026 [date to be confirmed].

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date. 

Please note that in submitting your application Durham University will be processing your data. We would ask you to consider the relevant University Privacy Statement Job Applicants/Potential Job Applicants - Durham University which provides information on the collation, storing and use of data.   

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

If you have taken a career break or periods of leave that may have impacted on the volume and recency of your research outputs and other activities, such as maternity, adoption or parental leave, you may wish to disclose this in your application. The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role.

Person Specification

Essential Criteria:

Qualifications

A good first degree in environmental engineering, microbiology, environmental science or a related subject.
A PhD in environmental engineering, microbiology, environmental science or a related subject.

Experience

Experience in conducting high quality academic research.
Demonstrable ability to write material of a quality commensurate with publication in highly-ranked journals.
Demonstrable ability to present research papers at international conferences and communicate complex information to specialists and within the wider academic community.
Hands-on experience of culture-based microbiology (e.g. selective plating, isolation and antimicrobial resistance screening).
Experience of metal and water chemistry analysis (e.g. total and bioavailable metals, nutrients, BOD/COD, organic carbon).
Experience of environmental field sampling, and of designing structured experiments or sampling campaigns.
Knowledge of metagenomics, bioinformatics and statistics sufficient to prepare samples and structure data for downstream analysis by specialists.

Skills

10. Demonstrable ability to work cooperatively as part of a team, including participating in research meetings.

11. Ability to work independently on own initiative and to strict deadlines

12. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

13. Excellent organisational skills, with evidence of planning and managing complex work, samples or datasets.

14. Ability to supervise and coordinate the work of technical staff.

15. A full driving licence valid in the UK or a firm commitment to obtain a license within six months of hiring.

16. Willingness to undertake outdoor fieldwork in the UK and to travel to India for one week early in the post.

Desirable Criteria 

Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals, commensurate with stage of career.
A track record of presenting research at conferences, symposia, or meetings, commensurate with stage of career.
Demonstrable ability to develop research proposals and designs in collaboration with other academics.
Experience of overseeing students with respect to the development of their practical/research skills e.g. acting as a demonstrator; supervising student projects/practicals.
Knowledge of mathematical modelling and/or economic evaluation.
Experience of working in low- and middle-income countries and/or in international, multidisciplinary teams.

A position exists for a Postdoctoral Research Associate within the Soft Matter Group in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics. The position is funded by a UKRI Grant titled "Nucleation and Extinction in Non-equilibrium Statistical Field Theories".

Progress in large deviation theory has created tools to address non-equilibrium rare events. We are currently extending these tools to field-theoretic models of the kind used to describe, for example, phase transition dynamics in active fluids; the invasion of a species into a new environment; noise-induced transition between attractors in fluid dynamics and/or ecosystem models; and noise-induced extinction of a population, gene, or behavioural trait.

The appointee will develop analytical and numerical tools to address rare events in various stochastic field theories. They will need strong familiarity with statistical field theory and at least some acquaintance with large deviation theory, or vice versa, and the ability to combine analytical and numerical skills to solve complex problems. We welcome candidates with an interest in ecosystem or population dynamics, and/or pattern formation far from equilibrium. The appointee will be working alongside two other postdoctoral researchers currently in place.

The role involves conducting original research in mathematics, developing individual and collaborative research objectives, proposals and projects, and disseminating research findings through presentations and publications. You will plan and manage your own research activities, contribute to collaborative projects and funding proposals, maintain and develop your specialist knowledge, and communicate complex technical material. You will also be expected to build internal and external networks and contribute to the wider mathematical community. The role may additionally involve supporting student research and project supervision, providing limited instruction, and planning and delivering research seminars.

Applicants should hold (or be close to completing) a PhD in Theoretical Physics, Applied Mathematics or a closely related field.

Appointment at Research Associate level is conditional upon the candidate being awarded their PhD. Candidates who have submitted their thesis but have not yet been formally awarded their PhD will initially be appointed at Research Assistant level and will progress to Research Associate level once their PhD has been awarded.

Informal enquiries can be made by contacting either Mike Cates at mec22@cam.ac.uk, or Rob Jack at rlj22@cam.ac.uk. However, we are generally unable to read CV's or other application materials before a formal application is made.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Closing date for applications is Friday, 15 January 2027. References will be contacted promptly upon receipt of applications, and all reference letters must be submitted by Friday, 22 January 2027.

Interviews will take place online in February 2027.

We welcome applications from candidates who are available to commence employment on or before 01 October 2027. An earlier start date, as early as June 2027, is preferred if feasible. Please note that the grant funding ends on 31 December 2028, with the duration of the appointment limited accordingly.

Please quote reference LE51584 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

About the Faculty 

The Faculty of Business and Law at Manchester Metropolitan University is home to one of the UK's largest business schools and to the Manchester Law School. The Faculty is committed to research that addresses pressing social, economic and environmental challenges, and works in close partnership with industry, policymakers and communities. 

About the Department 

The Department of Marketing, International Business & Tourism is an outward-looking academic community within the Business School. Among its research output there is a developing body of work on sustainable food system and public procurement, which examines how public spending can support fairer and more sustainable ways of producing and distributing food. 

This is a part-time post (17.5 hours per week, 0.5 FTE). The fieldwork will be carried out online, and flexible working arrangements can be discussed with the line manager.  

About the Project  

UK public sector institutions such as schools and hospitals serve millions of meals every day, which makes public procurement a significant lever for change in the food system. This project assesses the potential impact of sourcing public sector food from local suppliers, or from producers who can demonstrate high environmental standards. It considers the implications for regional economies, environmental outcomes and supply chain resilience. 

The project will draw on the experience of producers, processors and distributors in two geographically bounded UK supply chains to understand current practice in regionally focused food production and distribution. It will also identify the barriers to, and opportunities for, supplying public sector institutions. The findings will contribute to the evidence base on how public sector food procurement could be reshaped.  

The project is led by Adrian Morley, Research Fellow in Sustainable Food Systems.

About the Role & Team 

We are seeking to appoint a Research Associate on a six-month fixed-term contract to lead the project's qualitative fieldwork.

The postholder will conduct online interviews with around food businesses, including producers, processors and distributors, exploring their current practices and their experiences of, or potential for, supplying the public sector.  
Working under the supervision of Adrian Morley, you will take responsibility for the day-to-day management of the fieldwork and work independently to deliver it within agreed timescales.
The role offers a valuable opportunity to contribute to an emerging and policy-relevant area of research, and to develop your own research profile through the project's outputs.  

Key Responsibilities 

You will be responsible for designing and preparing the interviews, recruiting participants, and conducting and analysing the interviews.
You will consolidate the findings and work with colleagues and research partners to communicate them to academic, policy and practitioner audiences through reports, presentations and journal articles.   

Key Skills & Experiences  

You will hold, or be working towards, a doctoral qualification.
You will have research experience in business studies or a related field, including a clear, independent contribution to research projects and the preparation of written reports.
You will be experienced and confident in qualitative interviewing and analysis, and able to synthesise complex data and communicate findings clearly to diverse audiences.  
You will also bring sound knowledge of food systems, supply chains or sustainability.
As the role involves engagement with external organisations, excellent communication and relationship-building skills are important.
Experience of working directly with business representatives would be particularly welcome.

 At the Centre for Programmable Biological Matter, we are interested in understanding, designing and building natural and artificial bionanomachines. About the role

The Moore group at Department of Life Sciences, Imperial College London is looking for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to help develop new-to-nature antifungal natural products using Streptomyces bacteria. You will design and build engineered biosynthetic pathways, edit Streptomyces genomes, and scale production from shake flask to bioreactor, working alongside a collaborative team spanning microbial engineering, fermentation and analytical chemistry. 

Fungal and oomycete pathogens cause major crop losses and threaten UK and global food security, and growers have few chemical options because many are being withdrawn due to toxicity, and developmental fungicides typically degrade quickly in sunlight or soil. This project uses biosynthesis to access new-to-nature natural products with specific activity against crop pathogens and improved stability. The project will also involve co-supervision with Prof Tolga Bozkurt, an expert in plant-microbial interactions within the Department of Life Sciences, as well as Dr Marko Storch at the London Biofoundry.

You will join a diverse, collaborative group working on both basic and applied natural product biosynthesis, alongside postdoctoral colleagues on a parallel international project researching marine natural products, while the group also has regular visiting researchers from Brazil, South Korea and Europe. We encourage applicants with a strong background in some, though not necessarily all, of DNA and strain engineering, bioreactor cultivation and protein biochemistry to apply, as training will be provided. The group is also supportive of your own career development, whether towards an academic fellowship or an industry-facing route.

What you would be doing

Your day-to-day work will centre on three areas. First, DNA and strain engineering: designing and cloning plasmid libraries, introducing them into Streptomyces by conjugation, and editing the genome with CRISPR-Cas9 or directed evolution approaches to build production strains. Second, bioreactor cultivation: scaling production from shake flask to high-cell-density bioreactor conditions and developing fed-batch protocols, with access to mass spectrometry and proteomics facilities at the London Biofoundry for compound and protein analysis. Third, biochemistry: expressing and purifying biosynthetic enzymes and designing assays to characterise their activity, alongside purification and analysis of the resulting natural products by HPLC, LC-MS and NMR. You will also contribute to lab meetings, publications and grant writing, and will have opportunities to help supervise undergraduate and master's students.

What we are looking for

Essential

A PhD in biochemistry, chemical biology or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience.
A strong research track record, preferably with first-author publications in international journals.
Experience in molecular biology and bacterial genetic engineering, including DNA assembly, cloning and strain construction.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to organise your own work and prioritise with minimal supervision.

Desirable

Experience in the genetic engineering of Streptomyces or other actinobacteria, including CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and the heterologous expression of biosynthetic gene clusters.
Experience in microbial fermentation or bioprocess development, including bioreactor cultivation.
Experience in recombinant protein expression, purification and enzyme assay design.
Experience mentoring junior researchers, or working with industry partners or on patent applications. We encourage applicants with a strong background in some, though not all, of these areas to apply, as training in the remaining techniques will be provided.
Experience in analytical techniques such as HPLC or LC-MS for the analysis of small molecules.

What we can offer you

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity.
Benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days’ annual leave and generous pension schemes).
Access to a range of workplace benefits including a flexible working policy from day one, generous family leave packages, on-site leisure facilities and cycle-to-work scheme.
Interest-free season ticket loan schemes for travel.
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

This is a full-time fixed term position available for 36 months with a negotiable start date (Jan-Mar 2027). Appointments will usually be made at the start of the salary scale dependent on experience.

For informal enquiries please contact Dr Simon Moore (simon.moore@imperial.ac.uk).

Research Associate Biodiversity Science
Requisition ID:  29914
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Fixed Term
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  10 Nov 2026

Salary: £37,369 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 24 November 2026

 

The Role

 

We are excited to launch this new opportunity for a Research Associate in Biodiversity Science to join us in the School of Natural and Environmental Sciences. The successful candidate will join the TROPS research lab of Prof Marion Pfeifer, working with her on her new ERC project, TIF-CER, ‘From Forests to Fields to Sustainable Rural Landscapes: A Multiscale Framework for Quantifying Biodiversity and Climate Interrelationships’, running from January 2027 to December 2031.

 

In this project, you will work with Marion and the wider team to quantify how the three-dimensional structure and configuration of tree-based agricultural systems (trees in farms - TIFs) influence biodiversity and ecological functions, and how these functions translate into ecosystem services and disservices valued by different stakeholders. The project operates across multiple spatial scales, from individual trees and farm plots to landscapes and catchments, and across contrasting agroclimatic contexts.

 

Your particular focus will be on the biodiversity components of TIF-CER, including biodiversity responses to TIF structure and landscape configuration, mechanisms underpinning wildlife use of TIFs, and the potential for TIFs to contribute to habitat connectivity. You will work closely with the project's climate and land-systems science Research Associate to integrate biodiversity and climate perspectives and understand how these relationships change across spatial and temporal scales.

 

TIF-CER is working with partners in the UK, Italy, Philippines, Tanzania, Chile and Tunisia to:

establish an international network of field plots in TIFs and adjacent agricultural land uses and natural forests across contrasting agroclimatic zones;
quantify biodiversity and ecological functions associated with TIFs and establish mechanisms underlying their delivery across spatial scales;
analyse temporal trajectories of biodiversity, functions, services and disservices using co-designed scenario models of land-use and climate change; and
develop tools for end-users using robust evidence for decision-making on tree planting in farms.

 

The position is full-time (1.0 FTE) and involves substantial international travel, particularly during the establishment and implementation of the project's fieldwork programme. You will take a leading role in coordinating the biodiversity field programme across the international TIF-CER network. This will include planning field campaigns, coordinating equipment and field protocols, supporting local research teams, and training research assistants in standardised biodiversity data collection across different ecological and cultural contexts.

 

You will take responsibility for the day-to-day logistics of the biodiversity research programme, working with international partners to coordinate fieldwork schedules, equipment, data collection and field protocols across countries. You will also contribute to the recruitment and training of research assistants and local field teams and ensure that biodiversity data are collected consistently across the international network. You will be expected to co-supervise two PhD students and work with a diverse range of stakeholders to identify values associated with biodiversity and the functions that TIFs provide at different spatial scales. You will work closely with ecologists, land-system scientists, hydrologists, social scientists and local stakeholders to integrate biodiversity evidence with the wider TIF-CER framework.

 

We are looking for a candidate with strong ecological and quantitative skills who can combine field-based biodiversity research with spatial and/or statistical modelling, work effectively across disciplines and cultures, and take responsibility for delivering a complex international research programme.

 

What happens next

 

We are looking to appoint to both Research Associate positions by Spring 2027 at the latest, with the successful candidates expected to start as soon as possible thereafter, subject to the relevant contractual arrangements. We encourage candidates who are interested in the position to contact Prof Marion Pfeifer informally before applying to discuss the role and the TIF-CER project (marion.pfeifer@newcastle.ac.uk). As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf. These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Find out more about the Faculty here: Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering | Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering | Newcastle University

 

Find out more about School: School of Natural and Environmental Sciences | School of Natural and Environmental Sciences | Newcastle University

 

Contact for the post is marion.pfeifer@newcastle.ac.uk

 

Duration of post is 48 months, to December 2031.

 

Key Accountabilities

Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project.
Determine appropriate methodologies for research.
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations.
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination
Lead logistics
Present research findings, either at conferences or through publications
Contribute to grant applications submitted by others and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding.

 

Project specific key accountabilities 

Lead the design and implementation of biodiversity fieldwork (camera trapping, acoustic data collection, bird surveys) across the international TIF-CER network, including standardised surveys of biodiversity and wildlife responses to TIF structure and landscape configuration.
Take responsibility for the planning and coordination of biodiversity fieldwork logistics, including field schedules, equipment, protocols and coordination with international partners and local research teams.
Develop and apply appropriate ecological, statistical and/or spatial modelling approaches to quantify biodiversity responses to TIF characteristics and landscape configuration and to investigate wildlife connectivity.
Train and support research assistants and local field teams in standardised biodiversity data collection, including the use of appropriate field-based technologies and methods.
Integrate biodiversity data with environmental, climate, land-use and stakeholder data and work collaboratively across disciplines

 

The Person

Knowledge, Skills and Experience 

Strong applied expertise in biodiversity and/or ecological research, including experience of designing and implementing field-based biodiversity surveys and monitoring programmes.
Experience of analysing biodiversity data using quantitative, statistical and/or spatial modelling approaches, with the ability to work with complex ecological datasets.
Knowledge and experience of landscape ecology, habitat connectivity and/or the relationships between habitat structure, landscape configuration and biodiversity.
Experience of working with ecologists and/or researchers from other environmental disciplines to investigate ecological processes and temporal system dynamics.
Experience of implementing fieldwork in rural and/or tropical landscapes and working with international research teams, local stakeholders and/or communities to deliver field-based research.
Attention to detail and ability to work at high levels of accuracy.
Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences.
Proven ability to analyse data and write-up results.
Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues.
Excellent IT skills in all major office applications.
The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems.
Awareness of the research environment.
High level of analytical and problem solving capacity.
Ability to communicate complex information with clarity.
Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications.

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team.
Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines.
Commitment to continued professional development.
Understanding of good practice in equality, inclusion and diversity.

 

Qualifications

PhD in ecology, biodiversity science, conservation biology, landscape ecology, zoology, environmental science, or a closely related discipline.

 

Newcastle University is a global University where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.  As a University of Sanctuary, we aim to provide a welcoming place of safety for all, offering opportunities to people fleeing violence and persecution.

 

We are committed to being a fully inclusive university which actively recruits, supports and retains colleagues from all sectors of society.  We value diversity as well as celebrate, support and thrive on the contributions of all of our employees and the communities they represent.  We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams, we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and experiences reflect the diversity of our university and student population.

 

At Newcastle University we hold a Gold Athena Swan award in recognition of our good employment practices for the advancement of gender equality.  We also hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze award in recognition of our work towards tackling race inequality in higher education REC.  We are a Disability Confident employer and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role as part of the offer and interview scheme.

 

In addition, we are a member of the Euraxess initiative supporting researchers in Europe.

About the Role  

About the Role

Applications are invited for a Research Assistant in AI at the Centre for Clinical Pharmacology and Precision Medicine, William Harvey Research Institute. You will support NIHR Barts Biomedical Research Centre projects applying computational and AI approaches to cardiovascular research. Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will prepare and manage large-scale clinical, imaging and linked healthcare datasets, develop reproducible data-processing pipelines, and develop and validate AI-based cardiovascular risk prediction models. Research will focus on cardiomyopathies, hypertension and inherited arrhythmias, assessing model performance, generalisability and clinical applicability in real-world datasets.

About You

You will have an undergraduate degree in a relevant quantitative field, such as computing, mathematics, bioinformatics or statistics, together with a relevant postgraduate degree such as an MSc. You will have experience of undertaking a research or data-analysis project and strong computational, statistical and analytical skills. Experience of Python programming, basic shell scripting, and developing software, data-processing pipelines or predictive models is essential. You will be highly organised and accurate, with strong written and verbal communication skills. Self-motivated and enthusiastic about research, you will be comfortable working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team of clinicians, geneticists, data scientists and other researchers.

About the School/Department/Institute/Project

The William Harvey Institute is a world-leading centre for research, with a vibrant, multidisciplinary scientific environment devoted to therapeutic innovation in cardiovascular, endocrine and inflammatory.

A number of large-scale patient and cohort studies are taking place to address genetic, demographic and lifestyle risk factors associated with the cardiovascular system and develop new tools for improved disease diagnosis, prediction, and treatment. The Barts BRC at QMUL and Barts Health Trust will support and coordinate projects aiming to address challenges in CVD research and work in concert with partners at the British Heart Foundation (BHF)-NIHR Cardiovascular Partnership as well as the BHF Accelerator internally.

 The Department of Government and Public Policy at the University of Strathclyde invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to support and contribute to the ESRC project Disability and Political Parties (DISPOP), led by Elizabeth Evans (University of Southampton) and Stefanie Reher (University of Strathclyde).

 FTE:  1 (35 hours/week)
 Term:  Fixed term (24 months)

 The Department of Government and Public Policy invites applications from emerging scholars for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to support and contribute to the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) Responsive Mode project Disability and Political Parties (DISPOP). DISPOP is a collaborative project led by Professor Elizabeth Evans (University of Southampton) and Professor Stefanie Reher (University of Strathclyde).

 Despite reporting high levels of interest in electoral politics, disabled people are under-represented in legislatures around the world. To understand why these patterns occur, what barriers exist, and how to redress these inequalities, we need to study the relationship between disability and political parties - the key institution linking citizens and electoral politics.

 Political parties are important vehicles for mobilising and organising groups of citizens with an interest in politics; yet there are no studies focussed on how disabled people experience and perceive political parties, nor whether, when, and how parties think about disability, accessibility and inclusion. DISPOP aims to: (1) identify, analyse, and compare barriers experienced by disabled people, (2) map and evaluate existing party initiatives and best practices, (3) explore to what extent formal rules and informal norms render parties ableist institutions, and (4) co-produce recommendations with Disabled People’s Organisations to make politics more accessible.

 The University of Strathclyde is a leading, multi award winning technological university in the heart of Glasgow, one of the UK’s most exciting and dynamic student cities. Rated by the Daily Mail as the University of the Year for 2026, research is of central importance in everything we do. It informs our teaching and helps us to make a difference to business, industry and society as a whole. Almost 90% of research produced by the University of Strathclyde has been rated ‘world-leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’ in the UK Research Excellence Framework (REF) 2021.

 The Department of Government and Public Policy combines world-class teaching and research that explore political systems and institutions throughout the world. The Department has particular strength in the study of political representation of under-represented groups and quantitative research methods. The foundation of our work is a vigorous research culture. Our Research Excellence Framework 2021 submission was the highest-rated in the UK, with 62% of research rated world-leading and 100% of our impact rated outstanding.

About the Role

We are seeking a motivated postdoctoral scientist to join our interdisciplinary team tackling the threat of AMR in the human pathogen Clostridioides difficile. You will join the Clostridial Cell Biology Group in the School of Life Sciences at Warwick University and work closely with the biochemists, evolutionary biologists, bioinformaticians, statisticians and clinical microbiologists on the wider team in the Universities of Sheffield, Manchester and Leeds. We will analyse the propensity for C. difficile to evolve resistance to the frontline therapeutic vancomycin, the consequences, genetic basis and mechanisms of resistance and develop the evidence base needed to inform effective treatment in the future.

 

You will:

Be responsible for the molecular biology and experimental evolution aspects of the programme.
Lead on the writing of research publications and interim reports and prepare material and present at national and international conferences and research seminars.
Assist in the supervision of PhD, masters and undergraduate students.

 

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to  Prof. Rob Fagan  r.fagan@sheffield.ac.uk

 

Hybrid Working: Please note this is an on-campus based role due to the nature of the work, therefore we cannot accommodate any work from home basis

 

We and the wider University of Warwick environment offer substantial opportunities for professional development including regular opportunities to attend international conferences.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with broad expertise in bacterial molecular biology. The ideal applicant should have proficiency in:

Safe handling of HG2 microorganisms, sufficient to maintain the integrity of a long-term evolution experiment. Experience of anaerobic microbiology is a plus but not essential.
Purification and analysis of macromolecules including DNA, RNA and protein.
Cloning and mutagenesis of microorganisms using standard techniques.
Microscopic imaging of live and fixed bacteria using a range of imaging modalities.

Our £4M MRC programme across the Universities of Warwick, Sheffield, Manchester and Leeds brings together Molecular Microbiologists, Biochemists, Evolutionary Biologists, Statisticians, Bioinformaticians and Clinical Microbiologists to generate the crucial data needed to guide C. difficile treatment in the future. Role Description

A research technician position is available for up to 36 months to study the regulation, mechanisms and impact of a group of viriforms known as Gene Transfer Agents (GTAs). GTAs are descended from viruses that infect bacteria/archaea (bacteriophages), but they have lost the ability to recognize their own genome and instead package and transmit any DNA found in the host cell. As a result, GTAs could play a pivotal role in promoting bacterial adaptability, evolution, and spread of AMR. Their evolutionary significance is underscored by their conservation across alpha-proteobacteria for hundreds of millions of years and their independent, convergent evolution in diverse microbes, including spirochetes, firmicutes, and archaea.

Despite their clear importance, an urgent knowledge gap exists regarding the specific regulatory and mechanistic frameworks that govern GTA activity. This project addresses this gap through a multidisciplinary approach—combining genetic, molecular, structural, and evolutionary methodologies to:

Identify new GTAs in non-model organisms (e.g. in soil, marine, clinical environments)
Understand how they navigate complex environments like biofilms
Predict the impact they have on bacterial genomes and how they provide evolutionary benefits to their hosts.

You will be based in the Department of Biology, which is one of the UK's leading Biology departments, renowned internationally for our research. Experience of working on own initiative and as part of a team

 Role Description 

 The Hull York Medical School is seeking a highly motivated, forward-thinking, qualitative researcher to join a prestigious team to cover maternity leave. Work will directly shape public health interventions across the UK. You will be a key member of the Public Health Intervention Responsive Studies Team (PHIRST REACH)—a collaborative initiative led by the University of York in partnership with the Bradford Institute for Health Research, the University of Leeds and the University of Manchester. Funded by the NIHR, PHIRST teams provide timely, high-quality evaluations of public health interventions, supporting local authorities nationwide in making evidence-based decisions that improve population health. The post holder will be given responsibility to play a significant role in supporting the design and delivery of projects from a qualitative perspective.  

 Programme Manager and quantitative researcher to take play a key role in the planning, management and delivery of the evaluation projects. This will include qualitative data analysis, all associated routine reporting and dissemination of findings including producing high quality research outputs.  

 Role  

 The post will be appointed by the Hull York Medical School and will be based on the York Campus, within the Department of Health Sciences, whilst also maintaining strong links with the relevant departments across the Campus. The post is based at the University of York but may require occasional (subsisted) travel elsewhere across the UK to engage with local authority partners. You will be expected to work closely with the PHIRST leads.

 Skills, Experience & Qualification needed  

 You will need a first degree in health, applied health or psychology and a PhD in population or clinical health or similar discipline, or equivalent experience. You should also have knowledge and experience in a range of research techniques and methodologies, including study design, intervention development, co-design, with specific expertise in qualitative methods. Candidates are expected to bring demonstrable evidence of the ability to develop and deliver on research objectives, projects and proposals for own and joint research, with the assistance of a mentor if required.
